notes:
User is meal planning and prefers healthy, protein- and fiber-rich, reheatable meals. They recently received an Instant Pot and an Air Fryer.

Current meal plan:
- Cuban Black Bean and Rice Bowl, likely featuring black beans, onions, bell peppers, garlic, brown rice, avocado, and lime.
- Crispy Air Fryer sweet potato fries as a side.
- Refreshing fresh fruit salad as dessert, with assorted fruit, lime juice, optional mint, and sugar to taste.
- User asked about leftovers:
  - For the black bean/rice bowl, refrigerate in shallow airtight containers within 2 hours and use within 3–4 days; freeze for longer storage. Reheat only the portion needed to 165°F/74°C, adding a splash of water or broth if rice/beans seem dry.
  - Fries taste best immediately. Refrigeration softens them; freezing is better for longer storage. For safe storage, cool fries briefly (not indefinitely), freeze in a single layer before bagging, and reheat from frozen in the Air Fryer at 400°F/200°C until hot and crisp, shaking once or twice. Do not leave cooked fries at room temperature for prolonged periods or rely on a paper bag alone for multi-day storage.

Air Fryer fries discussed:
- Cut into uniform thin sticks, about 1/4–1/2 inch thick.
- Soaking 30 minutes can reduce excess starch, though thorough drying matters most.
- Pat very dry, lightly coat with oil, avoid overcrowding, and season after cooking or with salt near the end so it does not burn.
- Start around 400°F/200°C for 10–15 minutes, shaking the basket halfway; adjust based on fryer, thickness, and desired crispness.
- Potential seasonings include paprika, garlic powder, and chili powder.

Earlier Instant Pot interest:
- User is interested in pressure-cooked soups/stews, especially Korean Chicken Stew (Jjimdak).
- Ingredients: 1 lb bite-size boneless skinless chicken breast, 2 medium bite-size potatoes, 2 carrots, 1 large onion, 3 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp gochujang, 2 tbsp soy sauce, reduced gochugaru (user planned about 1 tbsp), 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp black pepper, 2 cups chicken broth, 2 tbsp sesame oil, optional green onions, and salt.
- Method: sauté sesame oil and chicken; remove chicken; sauté onion/garlic, then potatoes/carrots; whisk gochujang, soy sauce, chili flakes/gochugaru, sugar, and pepper; add broth and chicken; pressure cook and use natural release before opening; season and garnish. Serve with rice or noodles and optional kimchi.
- User had never cooked with gochujang and planned to use only 1 tbsp Korean chili flakes instead of the original 2 tbsp, then adjust to taste.
- Chicken breast can dry out; ensure it reaches 165°F/74°C. With dense potatoes and carrots, the previously suggested 10–12-minute breast-only pressure cook may not tenderize everything. Distinguish ingredient cook times and use a tested reliable time; natural release is preferable for continuing to tenderize potatoes. User had begun preparing ingredients.

Suggested brands:
- Gochugaru: Sempio or Koko.
- Gochujang: Sunchang or Chongga.
- These are commonly found at Asian markets or online.

They were initially concerned about spiciness because they had never cooked with gochujang, so they plan to use 1 tablespoon of Korean chili flakes instead of the original 2 tablespoons and adjust afterward. At the end of the conversation, they were beginning to prepare the ingredients.

Previously discussed recipe:
- 1 lb bite-size boneless skinless chicken (user chose breast)
- 2 medium bite-size potatoes
- 2 carrots
- 1 large onion
- 3 garlic cloves
- 2 tbsp gochujang
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp gochugaru (user’s reduced amount)
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 2 cups chicken broth
- 2 tbsp sesame oil
- optional chopped green onions
- salt to taste

Basic method discussed: sauté sesame oil and chicken; remove chicken; sauté onion/garlic, then potatoes/carrots; whisk gochujang, soy sauce, chili flakes, sugar, and pepper; add broth and chicken; pressure cook; natural release before opening; season and garnish. Serve with rice or noodles and optionally kimchi.

Suggested gochugaru brands: Sempio or Koko. Suggested gochujang brands: Sunchang or Chongga. These are typically available at Asian markets or online.

For future guidance, chicken breast can dry out, so verify it reaches 165°F/74°C internally. Also note that because potatoes and carrots are included, the previously suggested breast-only 10–12-minute pressure-cook time may be too short to tenderize them; a future answer should distinguish ingredient cook times and recommend a tested safe/reliable time rather than relying solely on chicken doneness. Avoid quick-releasing if potatoes need more cooking, since a natural release can continue tenderizing them.
